/-!
# Conjecture 7.56

by N. S. Chernikov

(B. Amberg). Does a group satisfy the minimum (respectively, maximum) condition on
subgroups if it is a product of two subgroups satisfying the minimum (respectively,
maximum) condition on subgroups?

A group $G$ is a *product* of its subgroups $A$ and $B$ if $G = AB = \{ab : a \in A, b \in B\}$.
The subgroups $A$ and $B$ are not assumed to be normal, so $AB$ need not be the join
$A \sqcup B$; the product condition is stated elementwise.

A group satisfies the *minimum condition on subgroups* if every strictly descending chain of
its subgroups is finite, i.e. the lattice of its subgroups is well-founded
(`WellFoundedLT (Subgroup G)`). It satisfies the *maximum condition on subgroups* if every
strictly ascending chain of its subgroups is finite (`WellFoundedGT (Subgroup G)`).

The two readings of "respectively" are independent questions and are stated separately.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

Does a group satisfy the minimum condition on subgroups if it is a product of two subgroups

That is, let $G$ be a group with subgroups $A$ and $B$ such that every $g \in G$ can be written

claims.decomposer_note: The 'minimum' reading of the 'respectively' pair: Prop is ∀ groups G and subgroups A, B with G = AB as a set product (every g = ab, i.e. ∀ g, ∃ a ∈ A, ∃ b ∈ B, g = a * b — NOT the join A ⊔ B, since A, B need not be normal), if A and B satisfy the minimum condition on subgroups (every descending chain of subgroups stabilizes, i.e. WellFoundedLT (Subgroup A) / (Subgroup B)) then G satisfies the minimum condition on subgroups (WellFoundedLT (Subgroup G)); yes/no question so use answer(sorry) ↔ …, G arbitrary (infinite allowed; finite case is trivial).
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same mathematics (elementwise or pointwise set product G = AB with no normality assumption; minimum condition = WellFoundedLT (Subgroup ·) on ↥A, ↥B and G; answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ G A B, ...). c05 chosen for style: `G : Type` and `theorem kourovka.«7.56».parts.i` inside `namespace Kourovka.«7.56»` match the existing Kourovka files, elementwise product is the most transparent encoding (c03/c07's pointwise `(A : Set G) * B = Set.univ` is equivalent but needs `open scoped Pointwise`), c01's `Type*` inside the ∀ adds a universe parameter against local convention, c08's nested `namespace parts / theorem i` deviates from the slot naming. Sanity-checked: hypotheses satisfiable (A = ⊤, B = ⊥), finite groups satisfy both conditions, and WellFoundedLT (Subgroup G) is provably the descending chain condition.

claims.reviewer_why: Same shape with WellFoundedGT (Subgroup ·), which by Mathlib's `wellFoundedGT_iff_monotone_chain_condition` is exactly 'every ascending chain of subgroups stabilizes' (the maximum condition). Stated as an independent question with its own answer(sorry), as the two 'respectively' readings may have different answers. Same style reasons as parts.i for choosing c05.

/-!
# Conjecture 7.56

by N. S. Chernikov

namespace Kourovka.«7.56»

/--
Does a group satisfy the minimum condition on subgroups if it is a product of two subgroups
satisfying the minimum condition on subgroups?

That is, let $G$ be a group with subgroups $A$ and $B$ such that every $g \in G$ can be written
as $g = ab$ with $a \in A$ and $b \in B$. If $A$ and $B$ both satisfy the minimum condition on
subgroups (every strictly descending chain of subgroups is finite), must $G$ satisfy the minimum
condition on subgroups?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.56».parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] (A B : Subgroup G),
      (∀ g : G, ∃ a ∈ A, ∃ b ∈ B, g = a * b) →
      WellFoundedLT (Subgroup A) → WellFoundedLT (Subgroup B) →
      WellFoundedLT (Subgroup G) := by
  sorry

/--
Does a group satisfy the maximum condition on subgroups if it is a product of two subgroups
satisfying the maximum condition on subgroups?

That is, let $G$ be a group with subgroups $A$ and $B$ such that every $g \in G$ can be written
as $g = ab$ with $a \in A$ and $b \in B$. If $A$ and $B$ both satisfy the maximum condition on
subgroups (every strictly ascending chain of subgroups is finite), must $G$ satisfy the maximum
condition on subgroups?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.56».parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] (A B : Subgroup G),
      (∀ g : G, ∃ a ∈ A, ∃ b ∈ B, g = a * b) →
      WellFoundedGT (Subgroup A) → WellFoundedGT (Subgroup B) →
      WellFoundedGT (Subgroup G) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«7.56»

items: 'G is a product of A and B' is formalized elementwise as ∀ g : G, ∃ a ∈ A, ∃ b ∈ B, g = a * b (set product AB = G), NOT as A ⊔ B = ⊤, because A and B are not assumed normal; this follows the decomposition notes.

Minimum condition on subgroups is `WellFoundedLT (Subgroup ·)` and maximum condition is `WellFoundedGT (Subgroup ·)`, applied to the coerced subgroup types ↥A, ↥B and to G. These are Mathlib's standard well-foundedness classes for the subgroup lattice; no bespoke definition was introduced.
Groups are quantified over `Type` (not `Type*`), following the convention of the existing Kourovka files (1_40, 19_25, 1_74, 20_76).
The two 'respectively' readings are given as two co-equal declarations parts.i (minimum) and parts.ii (maximum), each with its own answer(sorry), since the answers may differ.
Both slots are tagged `@[category research open, AMS 20]` per the stated open status.

reviewer_notes: No candidate omitted any slot and no candidate objected to the decomposition. The only genuine modelling choice is 'product of two subgroups' = set product AB (every g = ab), not the join A ⊔ B; all candidates made this choice correctly, in line with the factorized-groups literature (Amberg). Final file is c05's text verbatim; compiled with `lake env lean --json` producing only the two expected `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings. Attribution: module header says 'by N. S. Chernikov' (the proposer) and the docstring keeps the notebook's '(B. Amberg)' parenthetical.
